creator: Alexander Terp
description:
From #153, batch 9, item 5 (and the skill-doc side in batch 10).

`args:` and `command` blocks must precede every other statement. Breaking the rule gives errors that do not name it, and the two block types fail differently:

```rad
TOOL = "widget"

command go:
    ---
    Go.
    ---
    calls do_go
```

```
error[RAD10001]: Invalid syntax    (on line 1, TOOL = ...)
error[RAD10009]: Unexpected 'go:'
error[RAD10009]: Unexpected '--- calls'
error[RAD10009]: Unexpected 'fn do_go():'
```

With an `args:` block instead, the only report is `RAD10009: Unexpected 'args: name str'` anchored on the `args:` line, plus `Unexpected 'name'`. The reporter found the rule by bisecting; batch 10 says it cost two isolation rounds.

Wanted: one message naming the constraint ("`args`/`command` blocks must come before any other statement") anchored at the offending statement, without the knock-on parse errors (the cascade part overlaps bugfixes/a_28JrpwNqX).

Confirmed on main (3459ddf1).

Where: rts/check syntax-error interpretation (ERROR-node heuristics).
title: Name the rule when a statement precedes an args or command block
